why_angle: The cited B&H AK-R11 page and the cameraegg dome roundup price only the diffusers and assume the shopper already owns a V1. Neither gives a flash's output, its full-power flashes per charge or its cost per flash. This page compares watt-seconds, flash count, light per charge and price across the four Godox round-head flashes that take the dome directly. None of them is a product we list or an approved brand, and Amazon blocked amzcheck, so the page has no earning link.

page.title: Camera Flash with Diffuser: Godox V1Pro vs V1, V100 and V1 mid
page.h1: Camera flash with diffuser: which round-head flash to pair with a dome
page.desc: Four Godox round-head flashes that take a dome diffuser directly, compared on watt-seconds, full-power flashes per charge, light per charge and price.
page.answer: Short answer. For a camera flash with a diffuser, get the Godox V1Pro: its round head takes the AK-R11 dome diffuser directly, and its 76 Ws gives about 500 full-power flashes per charge. The 100 Ws V100 adds only 0.4 stop and drops to 400.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Light per pop. The V100 gives 0.4 stop more than the V1Pro or V1: log2(100 ÷ 76) = 0.40. The V1Pro gives about half a stop more than the V1 mid: log2(76 ÷ 55) = 0.47.
  • Light per charge. V1Pro: 76 Ws × 500 = 38,000 J. V100: 100 × 400 = 40,000 J. V1: 76 × 480 = 36,480 J. V1 mid: 55 × 650 = 35,750 J. The highest is only 12% above the lowest (40,000 ÷ 35,750 = 1.12).
  • Price per full-power flash on one charge. V1 mid: $179 ÷ 650 = $0.28. V1: $259 ÷ 480 = $0.54. V1Pro: $329 ÷ 500 = $0.66. V100: $349 ÷ 400 = $0.87.
  • Full-power bursts. Godox rates the V1Pro for up to 100 continuous shots at full power. The V1 manual allows no more than 30 in a row at 1/1, followed by at least 10 minutes' rest. That makes the V1Pro's rated burst 100 ÷ 30 = about 3.3 times longer.
  • Flash plus dome. V1Pro $329 + AK-R11 dome $11.90 (Pro Photo Supply) = $340.90.

Why more watt-seconds means fewer flashes

The V1Pro and V100 run on the same built-in 7.2 V / 2,980 mAh battery: 7.2 × 2.98 = 21.5 Wh. The battery holds a fixed amount of energy, so a bigger pop means fewer pops. The V100 puts 100 Ws into each flash and gets about 400 per charge. The V1Pro puts 76 Ws into each and gets about 500. Across the four flashes, total light per charge varies by only 12%. What you choose is how that light is split up.

The split matters with a dome fitted, because the dome costs light. In a bounce test with a Nikon SB800, SWPP's Mike McNamee measured about 2 stops lost to on-camera diffusers. Two stops is a quarter of the light, so 76 Ws through a dome lights the scene about as much as 19 Ws bare (76 ÷ 4). The V100's extra 0.4 stop wins back only a fifth of that loss (0.4 ÷ 2). That is why the V1Pro, with more flashes per charge, faster recycle and a longer rated full-power burst, is the better all-evening dome flash.

The round head does not cost output before the dome goes on. Fstoppers' Dylan Goldby metered a bare V1 at f/8.8 against f/8.7 for Godox's square-head V860II.

Set the zoom yourself. The Godox V1 manual says auto zoom follows the lens across 28–105 mm and says nothing about sensing a fitted dome. With the dome on, press ZOOM, set 28 mm and tilt the head up or to the side so the dome spreads light onto the ceiling and walls.

Not recommended

Avoid the Godox V860III if you are buying it to carry a dome. It costs $229 at MoLight and needs the $9 S-R1 adapter before a round dome fits, which makes $238. That is $21 less than a V1 ($259), which gives the same 76 Ws according to MoLight's listings and takes the dome on its magnetic head with no clamp.
